title: The COVID lab-leak idea is just a conspiracy theory
short_summary: In early 2020 major journals, officials, and platforms treated the laboratory-origin hypothesis for SARS-CoV-2 as a fringe conspiracy theory. Private contemporaneous records show leading scientists took laboratory scenarios seriously at the same time.
label: False
evidence_for: Very little primary scientific evidence in February–March 2020 forced the conclusion that laboratory origin was fringe.
evidence_against: WIV was already known to conduct research on bat SARS-related coronaviruses, including genetic manipulation, with U.S. funding via EcoHealth.
Early private scientific discussion (Andersen email; 1 Feb 2020 call) took laboratory scenarios seriously; Fauci’s diary confirms this.
U.S. Intelligence Community never treated lab origin as fringe (ODNI 2021).
No definitive intermediate host has been identified despite years of searching.

title: NIH has not ever and does not now fund gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology
short_summary: Fauci and NIH stated that NIH never funded gain-of-function research at WIV. The claim is contested because it depends on a narrow regulatory definition versus ordinary scientific usage.
label: Contested
evidence_for: NIH applied a specific regulatory definition tied to the 2014–2017 funding pause and later HHS P3CO framework.
Published genomic analyses conclude the bat SARSr-CoVs studied under the grant are genetically distant from SARS-CoV-2.
evidence_against: Documented construction of chimeric coronaviruses under EcoHealth → WIV subawards, including testing in human cells and humanized mice.
Ordinary scientific usage of gain-of-function covers deliberate creation of viruses with enhanced ability to infect human cells.
Congressional and later HHS actions (suspension then debarment of EcoHealth) cited material non-compliance around the same work.
The 2018 DEFUSE proposal from the same network proposed further enhancement work including human-specific cleavage sites.

title: The Lancet Letter (19 February 2020)
short_summary: Correspondence organized by Peter Daszak and signed by 27 scientists. Condemned conspiracy theories of non-natural origin. Published after private scientific calls that took laboratory scenarios seriously. Competing-interest addendum in 2021.
label: True

title: The Proximal Origin of SARS-CoV-2 (Nature Medicine, 17 March 2020)
short_summary: Paper by Andersen et al. concluding SARS-CoV-2 is not a laboratory construct. Most-cited early natural-origin statement. Drafting overlapped private Jan–Feb 2020 calls and the Lancet letter; FOIA/Slack show non-trivial lab-origin probabilities during drafting.
label: True

title: Peter Daszak
short_summary: Long-time President of EcoHealth Alliance. PI on the NIH bat-coronavirus grant that included WIV subawards. Organized the February 2020 Lancet letter. Debarred by HHS 2024–2025.
label: True

title: Jeremy Farrar
short_summary: Director of Wellcome Trust (2013–2023); WHO Chief Scientist from 2023. Central convenor of the early Feb 2020 origins calls that preceded Proximal Origin and the Lancet letter.
label: True

title: Kristian G. Andersen
short_summary: Lead/corresponding author of Proximal Origin. Central participant in the 31 Jan and 1 Feb 2020 private origins calls; early private communications assigned non-trivial probability to laboratory scenarios before the published paper ruled them out.
label: True

title: EcoHealth Alliance
short_summary: U.S. nonprofit that received NIH grants and issued subawards to WIV for bat-coronavirus research. Central funding intermediary. Suspended then debarred by HHS in 2024–2025.
label: True

title: Wellcome Trust
short_summary: Independent global charitable foundation (London). One of the world’s largest non-governmental biomedical funders. Jeremy Farrar was Director 2013–2023 during the early origins window.
label: True

title: Wuhan Institute of Virology (WIV)
short_summary: Premier Chinese SARS-related coronavirus research center. BSL-4 facility. Central node because of bat-CoV work, NIH subawards via EcoHealth, and location at the outbreak epicenter.
label: True

title: USAMRIID / Fort Detrick
short_summary: U.S. Army BSL-4 laboratory at Fort Detrick. Primary U.S. military comparative high-containment node to WIV.
label: True

title: Galveston National Laboratory
short_summary: NIAID National Biocontainment Laboratory. BSL-4. Documented formal collaboration and MoU with WIV including a memory-hole provision.
label: True
